To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) periodic frameworks are globally rigid in $\R^d$ if they are $(d + 1)$-connected and have redundant rigidity, (ii) the converse of (i) is true if and only if the framework is periodic, and (iii) periodic frameworks are generically globally rigid if and only if they are $(2,2)$-connected and generically have redundant rigidity.

(i) (d+1) connectivity and redundant rigidity of the underlying graph are sufficient and necessary conditions for a periodic graph to be globally rigid, (ii) these conditions are sufficient for a periodic framework to be globally flexible, and (iii) a periodic framework is globally minimally rigid if and only if it has a redundant rigid subframework and is globally rigid if and only it is (d+1 )-connected.

the conditions of (d+1) connectivity and redundant rigidity, which are known to be necessary for generic global rigidity, are also sufficient for generic global rigidy under fixed lattice representations for periodic frameworks in $\R^d$.
In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in order for a periodic graph $G$ to be globally rigid under fixed lattice representations, it is both necessary and sufficient that the underlying bar-joint framework be $(2 + \delta(G))$-connected and redundantly rigid in $\mathfrak{X}^2$, where $\delta(G)$ is the minimum degree of $G$.

the (d+1) connectivity and redundant rigidity of periodic bar-joint frameworks under fixed lattice representation in $\mathbb R^d$ are necessary and sufficient conditions for global rigidity in $\mathbb Z^d$.

a generic periodic framework is globally rigid in $\Bbb{R}^{d}$ if and only if it is (d+1) -connected and redundant, and if and only if its graph is a globally rigid graph in the sense of Hendrickson.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we establish the rigidity and global rigidity of periodic frameworks in $\mathrm{R}^3$ under fixed lattice representations and give combinatorial characterizations of globally rigid periodic frameworks in $\R^2$ under fixed lattice representation.

we provide the first combinatorial characterizations of periodic graphs whose generic periodic frameworks in any fixed dimension are globally rigid under fixed lattice representations in $\mathbb R^d$.

the rigidity theory for finite frameworks can be extended to infinite periodic frameworks in a way that preserves the rigidity conditions, the combinatorial characterizations and the global rigidity results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rigidity of infinite periodic frameworks is determined by a finite subgraph.
periodicity and redundancy can be exploited to simplify the rigidity analysis.
, in contrast to finite frameworks, the global rigidity of a periodic framework does not depend on the lattice in which the framework is embedded.
